stem.text: Use the limit comparison test with \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) to determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{6 n^{2} + 5}{4 n^{4} + 2} \), converges or diverges. State the conclusion, naming the series it concerns.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges.

worked_solution.text: Compare the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \) with \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), the p-series with \( p = 2 \), since the degrees of the denominator and numerator of the terms differ by 2. Both have positive terms.
The limit \( \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite, and \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges because \( p = 2 > 1 \).
\( \sum a_n \) converges, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges.

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) diverges, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{3}{2} \) is greater than 1.
options.derivation: the limit of the quotient compared with 1, as in the ratio test, and found greater than 1
